# Maximum allowed `pnpm pack` tarball byte count for the published
# `attaform` npm package. Enforced in `.github/workflows/publish-npm.yml`
# (the "Pack and enforce tarball-size budget" step). A publish run
# whose packed tarball exceeds this value fails before reaching the
# npm registry.
#
# Why a budget:
#   Sudden tarball growth is a strong signal of an accidental
#   publish-surface leak: a build artifact, a test fixture, or a debug
#   bundle escaping into the npm tarball via a `.npmignore` /
#   `package.json#files` mistake. Catching it at publish time means
#   consumers never pay for the regression and we don't ship an
#   `attaform.tgz` with `apps/site/` embedded.
#
# Why a committed file (not inline in the workflow):
#   Raising the ceiling is then a code-review event with a
#   justification in the commit message. The workflow file itself
#   stays untouched on size bumps. Same posture as `.size-limit.js`,
#   which fences the JS bundle byte budget separately (see "sibling
#   check" below).
#
# Sibling check:
#   `.size-limit.js` tracks the JS bundle byte budget — what consumers
#   actually parse and execute at runtime. This file tracks the total
#   npm tarball byte count — what travels over the network and lands
#   on consumers' disks. Different surfaces, both worth fencing.
#
# Current anchor:
#   v0.18.1's packed tarball measures ~1.46 MB (1456639 bytes). The
#   1887436-byte budget below is ~1.29× of that — tight enough to flag
#   an accidental publish-surface leak (a stray apps/site/ embed would
#   be an order of magnitude over, easily caught), loose enough that
#   ordinary feature work lands without triggering the gate.
#
# Editing:
#   Bump only with a clear justification in the commit message
#   (e.g. "raise tarball budget for the new <X> bundle"). The
#   workflow grep picks the first standalone integer in this file, so
#   keep comments above the number.

1887436
